bull.b: The Phase 2b psoriasis results provide meaningful clinical validation for ORKA-001, including high disease-clearance rates and no serious treatment-related events. If replicated in later trials, this profile could support differentiation, regulatory progress, and substantial commercial potential in dermatology.

Multiple clinical programs reduce reliance on a single asset and create several potential development and value-creation paths. Progression of ORKA-002 and ORKA-004 could strengthen the portfolio, extend the company’s opportunity set, and provide additional catalysts beyond ORKA-001.

Very low leverage gives Oruka flexibility to fund clinical development without substantial debt-service pressure. The reported cash and securities balance also supports continued investment in the pipeline and planned regulatory work, potentially reducing near-term dependence on borrowing.

bear.b: Because Oruka has no product revenue, its ability to become self-funding depends on successful clinical development, regulatory approval, and eventual commercialization. Until those milestones are achieved, operating performance will remain disconnected from sales and earnings visibility will stay limited.

Expanding losses indicate that research, clinical, and overhead investment is increasing faster than the company’s ability to generate income. Although spending may support pipeline advancement, sustained deterioration raises future financing requirements and increases the execution hurdle for achieving acceptable returns.

bear.t: Persistent Cash Burn And Dilution Risk
bear.b: Increasing free-cash-flow consumption means Oruka is using substantial capital to sustain operations and advance trials. Continued negative cash generation can require additional equity financing, creating dilution risk and making long-term shareholder outcomes increasingly dependent on clinical and commercial success.
